title: Mental subtraction: counting back and finding the difference

beats.say: Open like a teacher: two sums that look alike but need different thinking. Say we will learn two mental ways to subtract and how to choose. No questions.

lines.say: Here are two subtractions. They look alike, but they want different thinking. If you pick the right way, you can do both in your head, and quickly.

beats.say: Subtraction has two meanings: taking away (so we count back) and the gap between two numbers (so we find the difference by counting up). Explain with a number line. No questions.

lines.say: Subtracting can mean taking away. Then we start at the big number and count back.

lines.text: difference  →  the GAP between two numbers
lines.say: Subtracting can also mean finding the gap between two numbers, how far apart they are on the number line. Then we count up from the smaller to the bigger.

beats.say: Counting back for 74 - 13: split 13 into 10 and 3. Go back a ten, then back 3. No questions.

lines.say: Seventy-four minus thirteen. The number we take away is small, so counting back is perfect. We split thirteen into ten and three.
Count back the ten first: seventy-four, back ten, is sixty-four.
Then back the three: sixty-three, sixty-two, sixty-one. So seventy-four minus thirteen is sixty-one.

beats.say: Counting back for 81 - 76 would be silly. Show it, then switch to finding the difference. No questions.

board.text: When counting back is a bad idea

lines.say: Now eighty-one minus seventy-six. We could count back seventy-six steps from eighty-one. Seventy-six steps! You'd be there all day and you'd surely lose count.
But look at the two numbers. They're really close together. The answer is just the little gap between them.
So we count up from seventy-six, up to eighty-one, and count the steps. How? Next.

beats.say: Finding the difference by counting up in jumps, bridging a ten: 76 -> 80 is 4, 80 -> 81 is 1, total 5. Then 302 - 297. No questions.

lines.say: From seventy-six, jump up to the next ten, eighty. That's four.
Then from eighty up to eighty-one is one more.
Add the jumps: four plus one. The gap, the difference, is five.

The same trick works on bigger numbers that are close together. Three hundred and two minus two hundred and ninety-seven. From two ninety-seven, jump to three hundred: three. Then up to three-oh-two: two.
Three plus two, so the difference is five.

beats.say: How to choose: small number taken away -> count back; two numbers close together -> find the difference. No questions.

lines.text: Taking away a SMALL number  →  count back
lines.say: If the number you take away is small, count back.

lines.text: Two numbers CLOSE together  →  find the difference
lines.say: If the two numbers are close together, count up the gap.

beats.say: Do two TOGETHER. Questions written on the board first. Operands are written in the intro line.

lines.say: Now you help me with two. The first is ninety-three minus twenty-one, and the second is fifty-two minus forty-nine.
Twenty-one is small: back twenty to seventy-three, back one more to seventy-two.

ask.prompt: Which way would you do 93 − 21, and what is the answer?
ask.onMiss: Ask: is 21 small or big? So do we count back or find the gap?

lines.say: Forty-nine and fifty-two are close together, so we find the gap: one to fifty, two more to fifty-two. Three.

ask.prompt: 52 − 49: what is the difference? How did you find it?
ask.onMiss: Ask: are 49 and 52 close together? How far is it from 49 to 52?

beats.say: The child works alone: 85 - 12 and 100 - 97, then explain why they chose different methods. Hints only if stuck.

lines.say: Your turn to lead. Eighty-five minus twelve, and a hundred minus ninety-seven.
Twelve is small, so count back.

ask.prompt: Work out 85 − 12 and say which way you used.
ask.onMiss: Ask: is 12 a big or a small number to take away?

lines.say: Ninety-seven is very close to a hundred, so we find the gap.

ask.prompt: Now 100 − 97. Which way is quicker and why?
ask.lookFor: 3: the numbers are close, so count up the gap.
ask.onMiss: Ask: how far is it from 97 up to 100?
